entries.title: USAID enlightens women about energy conservation & opportunities in distribution companies (13302733465).jpg
entries.description: “These campaigns are an excellent opportunity for educating young women about to enter the workforce, about employment possibilities, while also educating them about their rights in the workplace, notably through the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act of 2010.” School Principal Rohila Akbar Four energy conservation campaigns were held at four women’s colleges of the LESCO region, where 1,200 students and 50 teachers were informed about Pakistan’s power sector. These activities aim to develop consumer awareness by involving female employees of DISCOs to inform and educate Pakistan’s female population about how to adopt energy saving habits at both homes and workplaces. The campaigns are targeted at women because as they take the message to “go green” to their homes, a ripple effect will be created that may help decrease the burden of the power shortfall at the grass-roots level.
entries.creator: USAID Pakistan

entries.title: USAID Power Distribution Program-Energy Conservation Seminar at Govt. Bukhari Public School for Boys, Multan. (8441773866).jpg
entries.description: Multan, January 12, 2013 - the USAID Power Distribution Program with the collaboration of MEPCO, held an Energy Conservation Seminar at Govt. Bukhari Public School for Boys, Multan. The purpose of the seminar was to: • Inform students about the USAID Power Distribution Program and the role of Distribution companies in Pakistan. • Educate students and teachers about the effective energy saving methods they can apply at homes, schools and workplaces. More than 2000 students along with principal & teachers attended the seminar & participated actively in the quiz session
entries.creator: USAID Pakistan

entries.title: Outer Banks Scenic Byway - Chicamacomico Life-Saving Station Historic Site and Museum - NARA - 7720864.jpg
entries.description: Scope and content: The original finding aid described this photograph as: Original Caption: This "life-saving station," with its decorative board-and-batten walls and elaborately styled eaves, clearly indicates European medieval inspirations for its designer, the architect Frances W. Chandler. It is the only one to survive unchanged of the first 23 built along the Atlantic coast in 1874. The boxy brown-shingled building to the left is an 1892 cookhouse. Location: Chicamacomico, North Carolina (35.596° N 75.467° W) Status: Public domain.
